title: Review
description:
A review attestation (join-spine `scenario_id` row: spec ↔ test ↔
ledger ↔ divergence). Mirrors the donor parity harness's required
review fields (`scenario_id`, `reviewer`, `pin`) plus its
provenance-ref requirement.

0.15 adds what the review saw and how the reviewer's run ended, all
optional and absent when unset, so a review written before 0.15
reserializes byte-identically:
- `pins` (D1): the scenario's source digest and its latest evidence
  records at review time. `canon review scenario` computes them; a pinned
  review only counts while both still match the corpus.
- `outcome` (D4): `signed` (the default, and what every pre-0.15
  review is), `indeterminate` or `unavailable`. Only `signed` is an
  approval; the other two are recorded gaps.
- `reviewer_provider`/`reviewer_model`/`reviewer_harness` (D4): the
  runtime that produced the review, as the caller reports it.

0.16 D5 adds `artifacts`: the files the reviewer looked at
(screenshots, recordings), stored like evidence attachments and
re-hashed by the gate. Absent when empty.

artifacts.description:
What the reviewer looked at (0.16 D5), each file stored in the
artifact store under its digest. Absent on the wire when empty.

change_id.description:
The change reviewed, on a change-level review (0.23): a chore's
sign-off, recorded by `canon review change`. Absent on a
scenario review.

code_tree.description:
The git tree id of the code the writing command saw (0.28 D7b):
the working tree for the default `HEAD`, the commit's own code for
an explicit rev; `.canon/`, spec roots and `code.exclude` are not
part of it. Absent on a record written before 0.28.

outcome.description:
How the reviewer's run ended (D4). Absent on the wire when
`signed`, so a pre-0.15 review (no key) reads as signed.

pins.description:
What the review saw (D1). `None` on a review written before 0.15;
`canon migrate` pins it (0.23), and until then it does not count.

reviewer_harness.description: The harness that ran the reviewer (D4), e.g. `omp` or `codex`.

scenario_id.description:
The scenario reviewed. Absent on a change-level review (0.23),
which names the change in `change_id` instead.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

worktree_dirty.description:
Whether the working tree's code differed from `HEAD`'s when this was
written (0.28 D7b). Absent on a record written before 0.28.

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

ChangeId.description: openspec change slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the directory name under `openspec/changes/` — joins: change ↔ tasks ↔ specs

CheckPin.description:
What one role's latest evidence for a scenario said (0.23 D5): its
verdict and the identity of the checks it bound. A report-backed
record's checks are `<format>:<case name>` for each matched case; an
artifact-only record's are `sha256:<digest>` for each file. New
evidence with the same verdict and the same checks is the same pin.

EvidencePin.description:
One pinned evidence record (0.15–0.22): its ledger natural key (the
`task_id`, else the `scenario_id`, it is filed under) and its 12-hex
content digest, together the record's ledger file stem `<key>__<digest>`.

EvidenceVerdict.description:
The three-way verdict an evidence record carries. `Divergent` is an
explicit third value rather than "no record exists" — the donor
parity harness represents non-faithful as *absence* of a
design-review/code-review record, which works for a directory-scanned
ledger but not for a single, standalone canon record whose own
`Deserialize` must always succeed or fail on its own — so canon makes
the state explicit instead of leaning on record-absence.

PinnedSpec.description: What a review's spec pin covers (0.15 D1).

oneOf.description:
The whole `.feature` file (`Scenario.source_digest`): any edit to
the file stales the review.

The scenario alone (`Scenario.scenario_digest`): only an edit to
the scenario or the context it inherits stales the review.

A change's brief (`brief.md` less its approval line): a
change-level review (0.23) goes stale when the brief is edited.

ProjectId.description: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` — lowercase alnum + hyphen, first character alphanumeric, no underscore (keeps the `__` natural-key separator unambiguous) — joins: not a join-spine key; composite identity prefix on Scenario/Review/Divergence natural keys (`<project_id>__<scenario_id>…`), optional on EvidenceRecord

ProvenanceRef.description:
Which provenance a `Review` cites — exactly one of the two ref
fields the donor parity harness's review-ref set (`upstream_ref`,
`original_spec_ref`) requires.

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

ReviewArtifact.description:
A file a [`Review`] binds (0.16 D5): what the reviewer looked at,
by repository-relative path and the sha256 of its bytes.

path.description: Repository-relative path, `/`-separated, as read at review time.

sha256.description: 64 lowercase hex characters: sha256 over the file's bytes.

ReviewOutcome.description:
How a reviewer's run ended (0.15 D4). Only `Signed` is an approval.
`Indeterminate` (the reviewer ran but could not reach a verdict) and
`Unavailable` (the reviewer could not run) are recorded so a failed
review is visible, never mistaken for a sign-off or a rejection.

ReviewPins.description:
What a [`Review`] saw (0.15 D1, reshaped by 0.23 D5): the reviewed
scenario's digest (`scenario_digest`, of the kind `scenario_digest_scope`
names) and, per role, what the scenario's latest evidence said — its
verdict and the identity of the checks it bound (`checks`). A new
evidence record with the same verdict from the same checks leaves the
review current. `checks` is written even when empty, so "pinned with no
evidence" never reads as "unpinned".

checks.description:
The latest evidence's verdict and checks per role (0.23). `None`
on a review pinned the 0.15–0.22 way, to evidence record ids.

evidence.description:
The evidence record files the review saw (0.15–0.22). Read only by
`canon migrate`, which rewrites the review to `checks`; the gate
does not count a review that carries only these.

scenario_digest_scope.description:
Which digest `scenario_digest` holds, so the gate compares like
with like. Absent means `file`: the review was pinned to the
`.feature` file's `source_digest`, the only kind before
`Scenario.scenario_digest` existed.

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

ScenarioId.description: `<area>.<surface>.<nn>` — `[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.\d{2,}`; never renumbered once assigned — joins: spec ↔ test ↔ ledger ↔ divergence

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

SpecDigest.description: sha256-hex: exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, over a `.feature` file's raw bytes, or over one scenario's normalized block and inherited context — joins: not a join-spine key; Scenario.source_digest (the inventory-sync freshness signal) and Scenario.scenario_digest (what a review pins)
